source_paper_text:
Let q be an indeterminate. For positive integers m,n and a vector (a1,...,an) of nonnegative integers define F(m,a;q)=product_{i=1}^n ((1-q^(m+i))/(1-q^i))^ai. Polynomiality means F belongs to Q[q] after exact rational-function cancellation.

Faithful mathematical restatement of Conjecture 4:
For every n>=1, every m>=n and every (a1,...,an) in Z_nonnegative^n, if F(m,a;q) is a polynomial then all its coefficients are nonnegative. No symmetry condition on a and no polynomiality requirement at other values of m is imposed.

title: Positivity for polynomial fake Gaussian products with m at least n
